title: Solver card
description: One solver's market listing for one network. Path: solvers/<network>/<name>.json

corridor.description: The rail a market side settles on. Absent means "arkade" (every spot market). A market with any non-arkade side is a corridor (RFQ) market: terms are negotiated per-trade via the card's discovery_pubkey + transports, not read from a price feed. EVM rails are named PER CHAIN rather than by a single "evm" value: a token address is only unique within one chain, so a chain-blind rail would let two different assets share a leg key. Adding a chain is a deliberate change to this enum, not a free-form string, so the reducer and every client agree on the set.

items.description: A Nostr relay URL the solver listens on.

nostr.description: Nostr transport config. `relays` is required; the object stays open to future nostr-specific settings.

transports.description: The v0 transport map. Nostr is the only supported protocol key.

id.description: Canonical asset identity: "btc", "native" for a chain corridor's own coin (ETH on ethereum), a 68-hex-char AssetId, or a lowercase 0x-prefixed contract address. The id is not chain-qualified by itself — the side's corridor names the chain and the leg key is "<corridor>:<id>", so one address on two chains is two markets, and "native" means a different coin on each chain. Lowercase rather than EIP-55 mixed case so the identity is byte-comparable; the checksum belongs to display, not to a grouping key. A bare name vs an address is also what tells a taker WHICH SETTLEMENT path a corridor uses, so the token standard need not be named separately: "native" settles as a plain value transfer of the chain's own coin (Boltz's EtherSwap), a 0x address settles through that token's contract (ERC20Swap). The 0x address is the TOKEN's address, never the swap contract's — a taker resolves the latter from the corridor, not from this field.

decimals.description: Decimals of the atomic unit: atomic units per display unit = 10^decimals. Matches the asset registry metadata field.

type.description: The price feed response is JSON.

price_path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the numeric feed value, e.g. /price or /bitcoin/usd. Empty string selects the whole JSON document.

amount.description: A canonical decimal-string amount of atomic units: unsigned, no leading zeros. "0" disables the side it bounds.

enabledAmount.description: An amount that is strictly positive: the side it bounds is enabled.

version.description: Card format version. 0 is every card written before EVM corridors existed. A card MUST declare 1 when any market side uses a corridor introduced after 0 (today: the EVM chain rails); a consumer that understands only 0 MUST reject a version-1 card outright rather than interpret the markets it recognises and skip the rest. Bumping is about INTERPRETATION, not encoding: the canonical form and signature are unchanged, so a v0 verifier would still compute a matching digest — and would then be trusting a rail it cannot settle on.

name.description: Unique within the network directory; must equal the filename (without .json).

discovery_pubkey.description: BIP340 x-only public key, lowercase hex.

sig.description: BIP340 Schnorr signature by discovery_pubkey over sha256(canonical_json).

transports.description: Nostr relay URLs the solver listens on. Required — with discovery_pubkey and sig — when any market has a non-arkade corridor (the reducer enforces this cross-field rule): they are the rendezvous makers address request-for-quote messages to.

pair.description: Display pair "<base-label>/<quote-label>", where a side's label is its ticker on the arkade corridor and "<corridor>:<ticker>" otherwise (e.g. "BTC/USDT", "BTC/lightning:BTC", "BTC/ethereum:USDC"). Must equal the labels derived from the sides' corridors and tickers (the reducer enforces this). Canonical identity is the corridor-qualified leg pair, NOT this label — note an EVM side's label carries its TICKER while its leg key carries the contract address, because a 42-character address does not fit a 16-character label and would not be readable if it did.

base_asset.description: Display metadata for the pair's base side.

quote_asset.description: Display metadata for the pair's quote side.

quote_corridor.description: The quote side's corridor; absent means "arkade". When exactly one side is on the arkade corridor it must be the base side (the reducer enforces this), so equivalent corridor markets group under one canonical key.

price_feed.description: Required when the sides carry different assets; must be absent (with the other feed fields) on a same-asset market, whose price is identically 1 — fee_bps and fee_flat are the whole price and executable terms arrive in the solver's RFQ quote. The reducer enforces this cross-field rule.

price_decimals.description: The feed value divided by 10^price_decimals is the price in quote-atomic-units per base-atomic-unit.

fee_flat.description: The part of the price that does not scale with size, in quote-asset atomic units. OPTIONAL; absent means none. Quote-asset in both directions, matching min_quote_amount/max_quote_amount, so a client converts it through the price when the maker receives base. Note that fee_bps alone is therefore not a ranking key: a market with a lower spread and a flat fee can be dearer at small sizes and cheaper at large ones.

min_base_amount.description: Lower trade-size bound for the base side, in base atomic units. An enabled side has 1 <= min <= max; when the side is disabled (max = "0") min MUST be "0".

max_base_amount.description: Upper trade-size bound for the base side, in base atomic units. "0" disables the side: the solver does not pay out base and makers cannot receive it.

min_quote_amount.description: Lower trade-size bound for the quote side, in quote atomic units. An enabled side has 1 <= min <= max; when the side is disabled (max = "0") min MUST be "0".

max_quote_amount.description: Upper trade-size bound for the quote side, in quote atomic units. "0" disables the side: the solver does not pay out quote and makers cannot receive it.
